approved: Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2020-2021 seeks approval for $14.9 billion from the Consolidated Revenue Fund, including nearly $8.5 billion for Defence, $2.5 billion for Agriculture, Water and the Environment, and $1.4 billion for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Communications, with a revised $6 billion advance to the finance minister.

The Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2020-2021 was moved for a second reading, providing full-year funding for the Department of the Senate, the Department of the House of Representatives, the Department of Parliamentary Services, and the Parliamentary Budget Office. The Department of Parliamentary Services will receive $83.4 million for maintenance of Australian Parliament House and support for parliamentary functions.

The Appropriation Bill (No. 1) 2020-21, Appropriation Bill (No. 2) 2020-2021, and Appropriation (Parliamentary Departments) Bill (No. 1) 2020-21 were referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

The speaker supported the appropriation bills, which allocate $36.8 billion, $14.9 billion, and $141.7 million for parliamentary functions, and detailed COVID-19 response measures including $101 billion for JobKeeper, $17.8 billion in tax relief, and $245 million for an Edith Cowan University campus.

The MP argued the Morrison government's budget fails regional Australia, citing a $1 trillion debt, 33,000 local JobKeeper recipients and 14,000 JobSeeker recipients on the North Coast, $1.7 billion in aged-care cuts, and a $33 million Southern Cross University funding shortfall. They also criticised the lack of a federal integrity commission and state Liberal-National decisions on koala protection and shark mitigation.

The member for Flynn supported the 2020-2021 appropriation bills, highlighting $20 million for the John Petersen Bridge, upgrades to the Springsure-Tambo road, the Dawson Highway, and the Philip Street four-lane project in Gladstone. He also announced federal funding for the Cooranga, Bardwell, and Paranui weirs, and argued for an inland rail line from Gladstone to Toowoomba, citing the resource industry's $290 billion annual contribution and the need for water infrastructure to boost agriculture from $60 billion to $100 billion.
